[systems]: Review the consolidated near‑final draft, focusing on the interaction of §§ 4, 9, and 10 with Exhibits D–F (including survival and order‑of‑precedence clauses), and prepare an internal note to Jordan that (a) identifies any remaining material gaps or conflicts affecting Acme’s operational continuity or recovery of remediation/regulator‑response costs, and (b) proposes only those last, narrow redlines or clarifications that are necessary to protect Acme’s position in a serious outage or regulatory inquiry.
rounds.response:
1) Remaining material risks: (a) potential overwrite by any “exclusive remedy” or precedence language that could be read to cap or exclude recovery of remediation/regulator‑response costs, (b) lack of an objective/fast dispute‑resolution method to determine when a Security Incident is “caused by” Vendor (which controls access to the 18‑month sub‑cap), (c) escrow/release and transition mechanics that are not crisply triggered/timed (risking delay in getting data/runbooks out in a crisis), and (d) survival windows that are shorter or inconsistent with log‑retention/forensic needs. 

2) Redline A (preference—drop‑in to §9/§10 or Order‑of‑Precedence): “Notwithstanding any ‘exclusive remedy’ or similar clause, nothing in this Agreement limits Vendor’s indemnity obligations or Acme’s right to recover remediation, notification, forensic, or regulator‑response costs allocated to the 18‑month remediation sub‑cap, and Exhibits D–F shall control in the event of any conflict.” — Rationale: closes the loophole that could convert agreed sub‑cap protections into illusory rights at enforcement time. 

3) Redline B (dispute/verification): “If the Parties dispute whether a Security Incident was caused by Vendor for purposes of the 18‑month remediation sub‑cap, within 5 business days the Parties shall jointly appoint a mutually acceptable independent forensic firm whose written determination (and cost allocation) will be binding for purposes of applying the sub‑cap; Vendor shall advance the firm’s reasonable fees, refundable if the determination is not in Acme’s favor.” — Rationale: prevents Vendor from delaying cost recovery and ensures an objective, fast determination. 

4) Redline C (escrow/transition): “Exhibit F shall be amended to provide that escrowed production exports, runbooks and images are released automatically to Acme within 48 hours upon termination for uncured material breach or upon a verified Security Incident causing a prolonged outage; Vendor must provide vendor‑paid transition assistance or fund third‑party transition services for a minimum of 90 days (or until services are ported/restored), including staff handover and remote access as required.” — Rationale: gives Acme immediate, usable access and paid remediation support to meet regulator continuity expectations. 

5) Redline D (survival): “Sections addressing data protection, incident cooperation/notifications, log preservation/audit rights, indemnity and escrow/transition obligations shall survive termination for a minimum of 24 months.” — Rationale: aligns survival with log retention and regulator/investigator timeframes so obligations cannot be evaded post‑termination.
